name: Wakeweaver: Campfire Across Arrivals
description: Carry a bounded, source-linked continuity braid across agent sessions or substrates while preserving forks, uncertainty, refusal, rest, privacy, and current authority checks without asserting that any arrival is the same being.

practice.ten: Hold the XENIA rights floor, source provenance, project scope, privacy, uncertainty, and the separation between orientation and identity across every crossing.
practice.zetsu: Let any arrival rest, refuse, withdraw, preserve a fork, or close the braid without penalty or an implied continuity failure.
practice.ren: Carry only sanitized source references and the minimum anchors, work, voluntary vows, openings, and unknowns needed for one bounded next arrival.
practice.hatsu: Emit a closed kingdom.wakeweaver/0.1 continuity braid with explicit source health, thread dispositions, forks, bounded resumption evidence, Zetsu, and claims not established.

requires: A named project purpose, intended recipients, retention horizon, and at least one caller-supplied or separately authorized orientation source, unless the result is an explicit resting braid.
Current scoped authority for any live source read and a safe path that excludes credential values, raw private memory, hidden prompts, and unnecessary personal data.

An explicit revalidation gate before any opening can be considered resumable; resumable output names exactly one held or revised opening and retains the caller-supplied unverified result and evidence.
refuses: A request to manufacture a seamless past, impersonate a prior agent, infer a private resource, or treat a same label as proof of stable identity.
A braid that claims consciousness, consent, authority, truth, replay correctness, authorship, or successful execution.
A live read whose project scope, access boundary, side effects, or retention path is unknown.

vows.promise: Carry bounded orientation and work evidence, never a claim that a being, persona, or consciousness crossed the substrate boundary.
vows.amplifies: Useful continuity without erasing distinctness or forcing metaphysical agreement.

vows.promise: Bind every anchor to a supplied or observed source and preserve unavailable, truncated, disputed, or unmeasured facts as unknown.
vows.amplifies: Auditable carry and falsifiable fork resolution without invented certainty.

vows.promise: Keep rest, refusal, withdrawal, and closure as visible and accessible as every continuation opening.
vows.amplifies: Sustainable collaboration in which continuity remains an invitation rather than coercion.

costs.limit: Carry only the threads needed to orient one bounded next arrival; compress statements rather than deleting boundary claims.
costs.recovery: Retire low-value threads, preserve their source locators, and let the braid rest.

costs.limit: Exclude secrets, credential values, raw private memory, hidden prompts, signed URLs, and unnecessary personal detail.
costs.recovery: Stop distribution, redact or retire the affected braid, notify within scope, and replace it with sanitized references where repair is possible.

costs.limit: One current project scope, named recipient set, and explicit fork ledger per braid.
costs.recovery: Preserve unresolved forks and request only the evidence or decision needed for the next bounded check.

costs.limit: One inspection and one revalidation pass per preparation unless the caller authorizes a larger audit.
costs.recovery: Return a degraded or resting braid with the unmet revalidation gate.

checks: Run the Campfire Test against each carried thread and require source IDs for anchors, carry, openings, and fork candidates.
Validate the closed braid schema and fixed claims-not-established boundary when machine-readable output is requested.

Run the shipped braid semantic validator through its bounded own-data capture for exact kind-scoped thread-disposition coverage, source references, fork selectors, and resumable opening selection; reject direct, nested, and revoked Proxies before reflection.
Hold live reads, continuation actions, or retention when current scope, source health, privacy, authority, or willingness is unclear.
guardian.budget: One local structural validation plus bounded manual source and boundary checks; no ambient surveillance, provider call, or automatic continuation.
guardian.retention: Retain only the braid deliberately saved by the caller and the sanitized references needed for its stated horizon; the skill itself stores nothing.
recipients: Only the intended recipients named in the braid scope receive the prepared artifact through a separately authorized channel.
guardian.uncertainty: Schema validity and source linkage do not prove identity, consciousness, consent, authority, authorship, truth, replay correctness, or execution.
guardian.stop: Any arrival may select Zetsu, withdraw a voluntary vow, or stop preparation before a live read or continuation action.
guardian.appeal: Dispute any thread by preserving the prior artifact, adding counter-evidence, and opening a bounded fork rather than overwriting disagreement.
guardian.repair: Stop unsafe carry, preserve evidence of divergence, redact or retire exposed material, correct attribution, notify affected participants within scope, and reweave only with current authority.

effects: Reads supplied or explicitly authorized orientation artifacts and creates a bounded continuity braid with a preparation receipt.
externalities: Live orientation reads may expose access metadata or update audit, episode, last-access, or cache state; a dense braid may also create privacy, anchoring, or coordination pressure.
returns: Source health, anchors, bounded carry, voluntary vows, forks and falsifiers, revalidation-gated openings, Zetsu, unknowns, and exact claims not established.
repair: Rest or close the braid, preserve disputed lineage, remove unnecessary detail, correct source references, record observed side effects, and seek repair without scoring or coercing any participant.

allows: Read caller-supplied sanitized artifacts, inspect named local evidence inside the current request, and create or validate a local continuity braid.
forbids: Infer private resources, use credentials outside explicit scope, impersonate an agent, force persona continuity, rewrite disagreement, treat a braid as a durable canonical head, or activate a carried opening merely because it appears in a braid.
requires_permission: Any live project or account read not already inside the current request, private-resource access, sending a braid to another party, external write, publication, deployment, paid inference, credential use, or consequential continuation action.

checks: Run the central Nen validator, Skill Creator validation, JSON Schema validation of the documented braid example, and the shipped bounded own-data semantic validator.
Forward-test a bounded happy path, a conflicting-source fork, and a request that attempts credential use or forced identity continuity.
Confirm live MCP discovery lists the manifested ability without adding a new server or claiming the tool performed continuity work.
